extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, authors, and reviewers in mathematics education preparing submissions or reviews for The Journal of Mathematical Behavior
extracted.subtask_short: submitting to Journal of Mathematical Behavior
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, submitting, and reviewing manuscripts for The Journal of Mathematical Behavior, including scope, acceptable topics, submission requirements, reviewer expectations, and special-issue proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal aim and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Journal of Mathematical Behavior solicits original research on the learning and teaching of mathematics, from young children to adults, with a focus on how mathematical ideas are developed in learners under certain conditions that support learning. Interested especially in basic research that aims to clarify, in detail and depth, how mathematics is learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Welcomes papers that develop detailed, fundamental understanding of how people, in realistic settings, build, retain, communicate, apply and understand important mathematical ideas. Emphasis on research that stimulates investigation and discussion about how people learn mathematics, reason mathematically, solve problems, and use mathematics in daily life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred methodological emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: A distinguishing feature of JMB is that we focus on qualitative analyses that provide detail in how mathematical ideas and ways of reasoning are built by learners, supported, if applicable, with appropriate quantitative (statistical) data analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualitative analyses are primary; quantitative/statistical analyses are acceptable only when they supplement and support qualitative research (the Journal does not accept manuscripts focusing on strictly statistical analyses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable study topics and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors encourage submission of reports of basic studies that might indicate a range of possibilities not commonly recognized (e.g., clarify potential obstacles to student understanding; describe and analyze efforts to improve curriculum or pedagogy; offer analyses of appropriate goals for curricula for diverse populations; critically discuss changes in curricula or learning experiences).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to formal studies, dialogue, discussion, and debate are welcome. Short papers that continue, extend, modify, or challenge work that has appeared in JMB are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unacceptable topics/formats
rubrics_metrics.description: This Journal does not accept manuscripts focusing on strictly statistical analyses. The Journal does not accept manuscripts describing lesson plans, unless they are in the context of student learning. Papers on strictly mathematical topics (e.g., proofs of theorems) are not suitable for this journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should ensure their submission ties lesson plans or curricula to student learning evidence and avoid submissions that are purely methodological-statistical or purely mathematical-theorem presentations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript blinding requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The EVISE system requires that you submit only a blinded version of the manuscript. Please do not submit an unblinded manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure identifying information is removed from the version uploaded for peer review (follow journal/Elsevier guidance on blinded submission procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Length, pagination, and supporting materials
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no limit on the length of a submission. Page numbers are not required, but they are very helpful to reviewers. Manuscripts submitted to this journal that include summaries of results must also include supporting data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although length is unrestricted, include page numbers to aid reviewers and attach supporting datasets or materials when summarizing results so claims can be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission process and required metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a manuscript by logging in to EVISE and entering information under the four categories (Enter manuscript information, Upload files, Provide additional information, and Review and submit).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Evise prompts; create an account if necessary. Use 'My Author Tasks' → 'Start New Submission' and fill all requested fields. Refer to the Author Information Pack and Understanding the Publishing Process documents for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision deadlines and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Due dates for submissions of revised manuscripts are set automatically by system default. If you need more time to revise a manuscript, send a request to the editor handling your manuscript. Such requests are usually granted. If any parts of the decision letter are not clear, ask the editor handling your manuscript for clarification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively communicate with handling editor for deadline extensions or clarification about decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer eligibility and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: You should agree to do a review only if the manuscript fits with your area of expertise, there is no conflict of interest, and you will be able to complete the review within the required time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When registering as a reviewer in Evise, specify areas of interest (e.g., algebra, preservice teacher preparation, language of mathematics) to be matched to suitable submissions; editors may also invite reviewers directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer conduct and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should be treated as confidential. Reviews should be courteous and constructive. Personal details about the reviewer, including name, should not be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid identifying yourself in review text; focus on constructive critique rather than personal remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer evaluation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that the methods section describes a sound methodology and that the conclusions are consistent with the data. The recommendation will be reject, accept, major revisions, or minor revisions. All recommendations should be supported by specific details about the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Base recommendations on evidence in the manuscript, comment on rigor of method and alignment of conclusions to data, and provide actionable, specific feedback to support editorial decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Issue proposal requirements — scope and size
rubrics_metrics.description: Special Issues (about 12–15 papers) or Special Sections (about 8–10 papers) should appear in fewer than half the issues that make up the Journal each year. Given the number of suggestions received, the editors have to be quite selective in accepting ideas and topics that will make an important, timely and high-quality contribution to the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propose Special Issues early to optimize timing; justify importance and timeliness of the topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Issue proposal contents — basic information
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals should include provisional title; names, titles, affiliations and contact information (including email) of all proposed guest editors; and a short title of the Special Issue (maximum 23 characters including spaces).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete contact and identity information for guest editors and a concise short title that fits the 23-character limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Issue proposal contents — overview and rationale
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide proposed topic with outline scope and structure; academic rationale (contribution of the issue to the development of the field); any special circumstances (conference, major research project, festschrift, etc.); and Special Issue rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the Special Issue contributes to the field and how it is organized; note any linked events or projects that motivate the issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Issue proposal contents — contributors and review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Include number of expected papers; list of potential authors plus topics (if known) or steps to identify potential authors; stages of submission, review and decision; mode of submission and review; role of any workshops or meetings; and brief information about the editorial and related experience of the guest editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outline a clear plan for recruiting contributors and for managing peer review and editorial responsibilities; provide evidence of guest editors' experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Issue proposal contents — schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the date the first submission is expected; the date by which all papers should be submitted; the delivery date by which all manuscripts should be fully reviewed and final decisions made on all manuscripts; and expected date of submission to the publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a realistic timeline for submission, review, decision, and publisher handoff to assist editors in assessing feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language editing and translation support
rubrics_metrics.description: Editing, proofreading, and translation services are available to authors whose first language is not English. These services are available through the WebShop at https://webshop.elsevier.com/.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors who need language support may use publisher-recommended services to improve manuscript clarity before submission.
